title: Maximize the Profit as the Salesman
statement:
A street has `n` houses at positions `0` to `n - 1`. Each entry `offers[i] = [start, end, gold]` is a buyer who will pay `gold` for the whole block of houses from `start` through `end` (both included); a buyer never takes only part of a block.

Choose which offers to accept so that no house goes to two buyers; houses may also stay unsold. Return the largest total amount of gold you can collect.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every subset of offers is exponential. Instead, walk the street from left to right and ask one question per house: what is the most gold I can have from the houses up to here? At each house either nobody's block ends there (the best total just carries over), or some accepted block ends there, and then everything before its `start` is an independent, smaller version of the same question.

## Approach

1. Group the offers by the house where their block ends: `byEnd[end]` holds `[start, gold]` pairs.
2. Let `dp[k]` be the best gold using only houses `0..k-1`; `dp[0] = 0`.
3. For each `house`, start with `dp[house + 1] = dp[house]` (leave this house unsold or not as the last house of a block).
4. For every offer ending at `house`, try `dp[start] + gold`: the block takes houses `start..house` and the best plan for the houses before `start` is already known.
5. Return `dp[n]`.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 5`, offers `[0,0,1]`, `[0,2,2]`, `[1,3,2]`. So `byEnd[0] = [[0,1]]`, `byEnd[2] = [[0,2]]`, `byEnd[3] = [[1,2]]`.

- house 0: `dp[1] = max(0, dp[0] + 1) = 1`.
- house 1: `dp[2] = 1`.
- house 2: `dp[3] = max(1, dp[0] + 2) = 2`.
- house 3: `dp[4] = max(2, dp[1] + 2) = 3`.
- house 4: `dp[5] = 3`, the answer.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + m) for `m` offers: each house and each offer is handled once.
- Space: O(n + m) for `byEnd` and `dp`.

## Pitfalls

- Use `dp[start]`, not `dp[start - 1]`: with the shifted index, `dp[start]` already means "houses before `start`" and never goes negative.
- Always carry `dp[house]` forward first; otherwise a house with no offer ending there would reset the total to 0.
- Several offers can share the same `end` (or even the same range); compare all of them instead of keeping one per house.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `byEnd` | for each house, the `[start, gold]` pairs of offers whose block ends there |
| `dp` | `dp[k]` is the best gold from houses `0..k-1` |
| `house` | the house currently being decided |
| `start`, `gold` | one offer ending at `house` |

narration.2: Make an empty bucket for every house so offers can be grouped by where their block ends.
narration.4: File the offer under its end house, keeping only what the DP needs: its start and its gold.
narration.7: dp[k] will hold the best gold from houses 0 to k-1; with no houses it is 0.
narration.8: Decide the houses from left to right.
narration.9: First option: no accepted block ends here, so the best total carries over from the previous prefix.
narration.10: Look at every offer whose block ends at this house.
narration.11: Accepting it earns its gold plus the best plan for the houses before its start; keep whichever is larger.
narration.14: dp[n] covers the whole street, so it is the answer.
